posts.name: Arcanist Lupus
posts.cooked:
Biomancer, Baron Blade, The Operative, La Capitan, and Bugbear vs Chrono-Ranger, Expatriette, Mr. Fixer, Tempest, and Argent Adept, in the TIME CATACLYSM.

 

Well, this is pretty intimidating, but I managed to come out on top.  Solid Mint, with everyone a little over 10 hp.

 

I did what I always do when I can and banished Chiquito to the bottom of Helena's deck using No Executions.  Atlantean Throne Room slowed the entire game down, except for Mr. Harmonious Tiger Claw Jackhandle Fixer, who doesn't care about royalty, or other defenses.  It did however, make everyone immune to the Surprise Shopping Trip.  Everyone, that is, except for Bugbear, who we had been instructed to take down By Any Means.  It turns out that Surprise Shopping Trip triggers a great deal in a five hero team villain game.  That took away over half his health.  Then La Capitan's Chronological Hot Spot tried to make Mr. Fixer deal himself 3 damage.  Or in this case, blindly lash out at all the villains for 4 irreducible.  Tempest managed to chain his Gene-Bound Shackles, AA let Mr. Fixer play another Overdrive, and the only villains left were Biomancer and Baron Blade, each at 1.  A little Opressive Smog meant that they stayed at 1, and Chrono-Ranger kept his Eyes on the Prizes, and finished them off.

posts.name: Reverend Pete
posts.cooked:
Mint.

 

It was a skin of the teeth situation, though.  Atlantean Throne Room, Oppressive Smog and Jack Handle/Tiger Claw is what did it.  Otherwordly Resilience kept Tempest alive and helpful. Chrono-Ranger did quite a bit of damage too, before he went down at the end.  Argent Adept was taken out relatively early...I think either right before or right after Bugbear went out.

 

Misplayed a couple of things, like accidentaly boosting Argent Adept's damage (?!) instead of Tempest's with a Syncopated Onslaught and I kept using choose for me for area damage, only to realize that I should hit Chiquito first when he's got one card under him, instead of La Capitan.  I think that kept her alive longer than she otherwise would have been. And I never learned from my mistake. I think I did it almost every time.

 

As a result, La Capitan was the last villain to fall. It was close: Chrono-Ranger, Expatriette and Argent Adept were incapped, Mr. Fixer at 1HP and Tempest at 5HP.

posts.cooked:
scifantasy:

and I really should have focused more on Bugbear. Didn't realize how dangerous he was at first.

 

Always, always, ALWAYS rush Bugbear first. Every incap gives him not only more damage but feeds his life steal making him more and more unkillable. And once you start on him you have to continue the pressure or he'll just heal it back up. Pretty much the only thing that's higher priority are targets that hamper your ability to deal damage/keep things in play, and Steel's Agents.

posts.name: bolnerap
posts.cooked:
Relatively easy Mint, final HP 4/8/7/4/7 due to the complete and total lack of healing. But the lack of healing due to the eventual environment shutdown hurt the enemy far, far more than it hurt me.

My round 1 plan went sideways when the villains played multiple forms of Ongoing destruction, so I spent round 2 doing other stuff and round 3 getting my plan re-set in motion thanks to Vernal Sonata. After three rounds, Fixer was set up for good with Jack Handle, ATC, and Harmony, and everyone else did what they could.

CR only saw two copies of Sudden Contract and never saw a bounties-from-trash card, so I had to make do with only By Any Means and No Executions. BAM was enough to get Bugbear dead in the round that Surprise Shopping Trip came out - he killed himself with his card play that round. No Executions shut down La Capitan, as others have noted.

Expat spent several turns using Arsenal Access until I started getting a hand full of Ammo. Three consecutive rounds of an Assault Rifle with Hollow Points (thanks, Fixer, for digging ammo out of the trash) was key in whittling down Operative/LC/Blade.

Tempest destroyed Ongoings and generally did a whole bunch of damage until the Throne Room came out, then he eventually drew some more damage one-shots.

AA mostly destroyed ongoings until he eventually had the chance to pass card plays around. Ruin came out early, so I never bothered playing any instruments.

 

Kill order was Bugbear, then LC/Operative in one round later, then Blade/Biomancer one round after that.
